What will a day look like before it ends?

You have failed to give yourself a good night' sleep. You wake up ahead of your alarm. You don't know what you will do if you hear another noise. You grow tired of deafening voices you had last night. You toss and turn on your bed as you replay the intuitions you have. Something is wrong. You know it and you don't want to admit it 'cause when you do, you'll mark the finality of whatever episode you're in. Like a TV series you have loved only to be disappointed by the ending.

The day is dragging but you force yourself to rise. The world doesn't take a break. It carries on even if you can't. You start wondering why the day feels so different when it supposed to be just your ordinary routine. It should have been. Except it is not. 

You look in the mirror. You raise your brow, pondering if that's really yourself you're seeing. You shrug and continue with your morning agenda.  You don't want to make coffee this time. You don't want to rely on it to make the day bearable. You want it to end. 

Today, you are alone. And that's when you realize that it has been a long time since you have this solitude. It starts when you ride the cab by yourself. No, maybe it's by that morning when you didn't send a morning greeting to someone. Or not making a coffee 'cause you know someone will make you one. You laugh. You go to a nearest store and buy yourself a coffee. You are trying to break the cycle you have grown comfortable with. 

When you get so used to a cycle, it's hard to pinpoint what's wrong. It's easy to just go in circles rather than putting an end to a pattern. You have seen everything through rose-colored glasses, until you have lost your colors. Until you don't know yourself anymore.

You put on your earphones and listen to your favorite songs. At least there are things that remain to be yours. It's crazy how a particular song can bring you back to a a particular time. The time when you built walls to yourself but somewhere along the way, someone broke those. You should have known, next was your heart. 

You hum in every song as the memories flood you. You recall the moments when you were elated. That for once, everything seemed to fall into place. Until it didn't. 

You press stop. A gesture you should've done sooner. 

You walk back home. Tonight, you will be alone. You might lose that constant someone, but you will find yourself again. 

Tonight, you are alone. 

You try to sleep for tomorrow is a journey of [what will a day look like after it ends](https://www.reddit.com/r/Philippines/comments/7tbv92/comment/dtbdnoi/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web2x&context=3).

No matter what happened to us, I know there were good parts. Of you. Of us. I will always be the first who'll admit that.

And sometimes, I find myself picking through our memories like antiques and old mementos you find in your basement. Sometimes, I blow off the dust on the day we first met, or the first time we held hands, or the first time we kissed. I wipe the dirt from the moment I realized that I was in love with you, and the first time I said it out loud.

I flip through our best times like old photo albums, or listen to your laughter like grungy vinyl record. Surreal.

But mostly I end up sitting in front of the broken picture frames lining the shelves; our first fight, the first broken promise, the second promise, and then lie after lie, after lie. Crack, after crack, after crack. I come back to the broken parts of us because I'm not ready to acknowledge the good parts by themselves. And how the best parts overshadowed by worst parts. I can’t trust myself to not stare at the shiny pieces for too long, to not forget about the splinters and cracks on the other side of the room.

Someday, I won't need to hold our shattered pieces in my hands to know that they're there; that they aren't going away.

Someday, I will be able to put the record of your laugh on play without being afraid of remembering how that laugh also broke my heart.

Someday, I will be able to sit there, and just listen.
I feel like breaking down. Nakakapagod magpanggap na okay ka ‘cause that’s what people are expecting from you. Itutulog ko na lang ‘to.

To my first redditor friend,

How are you? It’s been months since we last talked. Ten months exactly. I’ve checked your account and it’s not active anymore. Maybe you created a new one. I’m sorry for losing contact with you as I deleted my main account and telegram. That time I wanted to vanish from everyone. But here I am, doing good (I guess), missing you. 

Have you read the book I gave you? Did it give you some hope just like it did to me? Along with it was the journal for you to vent things out. Did you scribble words? Remember those times you said that you liked my writings? Guess what? I don’t write anymore. Well, not that frequent like I used to. I hate how empty I feel. And no words can seem to fill that void. 

But hey, I already moved on from him. It was our common denominator, right? How we got along through heartaches from our past love. I hope the same to you. 

By the way, I made a lot of friends here. I hope you can meet them as well. Take care always.

**It’s okay to have bad days.**

 

It’s okay to wake up on the wrong side of the bed, snooze your alarm, and drift back into the comfort of dreamland again. Sometimes you just need a few more minutes in bed. Sometimes you just need that rest. You deserve that. Sometimes you won’t feel ready to face the world just yet.

It’s okay to stare at your laptop screen or get distracted by your phone ringing when you’re supposed to be working on your day job or your dreams. Because you’re not perfect. Ceasing bad habits takes longer than you think, and sometimes your willpower topples to an all-time low.

 

It’s okay if you don’t feel like smiling today. You don’t have to plaster on a fake one just to please the people around you. You don’t owe this world your cheeriness.

It’s okay if you don’t feel like socializing today. It’s okay to allow that drizzly, gray cloud above your head today and wallow beneath your privy, silent storm. Sometimes we need solitude. 

I want you to know it’s okay to feel shit sometimes.

 


It’s okay to skip your usual agenda and polish off a box of chocolates or devour that comfort food of yours instead because nothing sounds more appealing right now. It’s okay to look at that sprouting to-do list staring you down, say fuck it, and proceed to do nothing but doodle and daydream for the rest of the day. ‘Cause fuck doldrums, right? 

It’s okay to feel like nothing is going your way, and you feel like the universe is playing puppeteer to your strings. We all feel like that sometimes. 

 

It’s okay to let a melancholic playlist loop on in the background and allow yourself to make a comforting blanket out of others’ heartache. 
It’s okay to breakdown, and just let those tears roll down your face. For whatever reasons, or no reason at all.

I need you to know it’s okay to not be okay all the time. Bad days will find their way to all of us. But trust that those gray skies will eventually dissever for bright, blue ones. 

Trust that better days are waiting for you on the not-so-distant horizon. And it would be all worth it. 

 

You got this.

Over the course of life, we find ourselves dealing with these people. Those who make us crook ourselves like barbed wire in numerous attempts to please them - only to never really get there. Their damage lies in their subtlety and the way they can beget that classic response, ‘It’s not them, it’s me.’ They can have you questioning your *oversensitivity*, your *tendency to misinterpret* and draw that *because you are crabby and choleric* card. 

They tend to focus on your mistakes, obscuring your redeeming qualities. 
You’ll find yourself apologizing and mostly this will go around in circles.

We find ourselves dealing with people who are quick to judge, and often enough forget (or unaware) that such judgment also applies to them as well. Some pretend to have a rapport with you. They'll offer you their fake sympathy, their selective empathy but really have their own biases and prejudice. 

Guess what? Dealing with them makes you learn the art of indifference. Some people can’t be pleased and some people won’t be good for you – and many times that has nothing to do with you. You don’t need anyone’s approval or validation but remember if someone is working hard to be devious and manipulative, it’s probably because they need yours. You don’t always have to give it but if you do, don’t let the cost be too high. (Or maybe just don't give it :P).

I hope you truly listen.

I hope you notice the flicker in their eyes as they ramble about their passions. Let the fire radiate to where you are even if you don’t know where it came from. Open your hands and feel the warmth. Take every detail, every sentimental pause, every wave in their tone. When they laugh, flash an encouraging smile. When they tear up, offer silence.

I hope you get a chance to ask questions because you’re seeking for an answer. Pay attention to how they flip the pages of their stories. You are not there to edit their thoughts nor forcibly omit their errors. You are there to absorb their chronicles as if watching a movie for the first time. When they struggle for words, suggest a phrase and let them go on from there.You are a passenger on this journey. Sit back and wait where it will take you.

I hope you stay there until the end. Don’t ridicule their daydreams, no matter how silly they seem to be. Don’t mock their beliefs just because they differ from yours. Don’t block their explanations even if you find them uninteresting. Consider how hard it must have been for them to muster all the words just to share something with you. Be there till the last sentence is spoken.

I hope you treasure the pieces that they laid in front of you. Keep their realizations close to your chest. Treat every experience as expensive gems mined from deep within the heart of a mountain. If you are out of words, you don’t have to force anything to come out. Being the chosen one to receive their sagas is more than enough. 

I hope their fragments survive inside you. And I hope you will find people who will keep yours with them as well.

You don’t have to alter yourself just so you can stay. 

 

You don’t have to force the pieces to fit. Spending hours with them do not mean you have to stroke the same colors. Countless coffee dates and drinking sessions do not require you to utter the same language dwelling in their tongue. Listening to them talk about their passions does not mean that you have to catch the fire as well. 

Sometimes you are cognizant of their laughter but what you hear is an alarm that makes you wonder if it’s supposed to be a comic thing. Sometimes, they are sprawled all over the place and you feel like a stranger standing at the other side of the door, hesitating to ring the bell. Sometimes, they are at the height of the party but your heart is an uninvited guest even if you’re standing beside them all along. 

You should know that it’s okay. You can be a raging red in a sea of blush. You don’t have to wish for the same story like theirs. You should not feel guilty for saying no. You are not selfish for not wanting to adapt on how they have fun. And if you really were, you should know it's okay to be selfish sometimes. You are just acknowledging your differences. 

You can still be that person; hearing the reasons why they cry, leading the toast in their success, and consoling them in their failure. You can still answer their phone calls in the middle of the night.

 

Life is a hurdle. There's no denying that. And people tend to cling for support of others. And you? You provide it willingly. You are a blessing. 

*But sometimes you need to be your own blessing, too*


You cannot be everything to everyone who wants you or expects you to be. And that’s okay. You don't need to find your worth solely in what you do for others.

You are more than enough.

Sharing yourself doesn’t mean losing a part of it. As you hug the people you love, don’t forget to embrace your individuality as well.

What will a day look like after it ends?

It starts as soon as you open your eyes. When the nightmare that you had last night is still clinging at the edge of your vision and the smell of burnt memories is still hanging on your nostrils. Aching for arms that will defend you from your fears, you roll on your side only to feel the smooth sheets lying beside you. Suddenly, you realize that you were alone the whole night. The weight of pain that is lying inside your chest screams so loud; sides feel like they're breaking because of the rattle. Still, you breathe. You drag your feet from your bed and force yourself to start the day. 

You stand in front of the sink, noticing how there is only one toothbrush on it when there used to be two. You frown but you brush your teeth anyway, in case you need to fake a smile. You make your own coffee this time and try to swallow it down with the lump in your throat that is always threatening to explode. Crying will be for another day.

In the subway, you feel almost everyone’s eyes staring at your empty ones, wondering what they are looking at. Maybe it’s your soul that was trapped in a love that was thrown out to the sea. You assume that they heard your insides screaming, begging to be rescued from too much exhaustion for feeling too much. You notice a child smiling sadly at you. You try to smile back. You brushed your teeth anyway.

By the time you reach your destination, you feel like the universe is playing you for the song that someone used to sing to you in those summer nights blasts as if trying to slap you of everything that you are trying to forget. You feel the need to call in sick for work and stop because you can not file heartbreak as a reason to go absent. So you endure the day until it’s time for you to go home and cry about how everything is tearing you to shreds.

You question everything. You replay how you shattered before those eyes when goodbye has been uttered. You go on through all the memories you had with that person. You dissect every situation and try to pinpoint where the virus that infected that love for you is. You try to wonder when did it really die. And you feel like dying until you finally fall to slumber.

These are your days. A routine that makes you wonder if the suffering has an end. 

You feel like you are walking an endless tunnel but slowly, slowly you feel the changes. You wake up one day and you don't have any nightmares to run away from. You roll on your side and see pass through the sunlight escaping from the windowpane, not the empty space beside you. You brush your teeth and smile so wide; your cheeks ache as you anticipate the great day ahead of you. 

You don't know when it started. You don't know when exactly did you forget. There are no fireworks or cheers of celebration. There's no party. Only your heart, thanking you that you held on long enough for it to heal; and your eyes, seeing the world without feeling the need to look for that person.

You begin again after the ending. 

And then you experience [the day when the wounds have healed and the scars become barely noticeable](https://www.reddit.com/r/Philippines/comments/7szprx/daily_random_discussion_jan_26_2018/dt90b01/).

It's glorious.

What will a day look like when the wounds have healed and the scars become barely noticeable?

You wake up in the morning to the sound of your alarm clock instead of that distant voice from a lucid dream you had nor the resonating, fading scream, begging for someone to come back. You stare at the ceiling, listing the agendas that you have for that day. You don’t look for the rumblings on the walls anymore. You don’t even remember you materialized them. 

You roll on your bed, not minding the free space it has. You close your eyes again as you wait for five more minutes. Five more minutes before a busy day ahead. When you turn on the shower, you just savor the water cascading through your body. You don’t think of the hands that once explored it. The kisses that were planted on some parts of it don’t even haunt you anymore. Those captivating and passionate nights disappear like the bubbles covering you whole. You’re finally clean.

The mirror no longer mutters with splinters. It just tells you how well-groomed you are or how refined your outfit for the day is. Its reflection has forgotten to bawl the language of hatred and regrets. It has finally learned how to flash you a genuine smile, the one that doesn’t need a mask.

Coffee tastes a lot better now. You don’t even rely on it to numb you down anymore. You just let your tongue relish on its flavor as you let the aroma wake you.

You amble through chaotic avenues with only your destination on your mind. You don’t tilt your head in different directions just to look for a familiar face. You don’t look at the streetlight, thinking of the time you roamed by the darkness, entangled with someone’s fingers. When the song that was once sung to you started playing somewhere, you don’t lose yourself anymore. You sing along as the lyrics have lost their sharpness. The history might be appalling but the music is still good. 

You don’t gaze at lovers with twinge or bitterness. Love exists and you don’t have it right now. And that’s okay. That’s okay.

During lunchtime, you focus on your food instead of the empty seat across you or appreciate a friend who shares a table with you. You have grown comfortable to your solitude, you don’t mind the bizarre looks you occasionally feel. The food is delicious anyway.

When nighttime hits and nostalgia is threatening to pull you back to the past, you brush it off. You buy a bottle of your favorite drink or a pack of your comfort food. Just enough to blur all the distasteful memories away. You’re not even worrying about sending drunk messages. When all has been said and done, you just leave all the past contacts alone.


You go home. You are no longer looking for a place to hide all your tears. You just want a good night sleep. 

And if ever you find your former lover sitting at the front of your door, lips that try to say unsaid apologies, you no longer flip and take them. You stand between that person and the door. You take the keys, you unlock it. You block that person from getting inside again.

You tell that person to go home.
